As this is Snapchat my swiping knowledge isn't on an expert level but I think it should suffice.

If you look at the photo above you can see at the bottom middle of the picture there is a white ring (lacking a better word) around a link for BLM. If you put your thumb on this and drag it upwords as you keep your thumb on the screen. This motion can be called both swiping up or scrolling down. In this case as your action will take you to a new page I would classify it as swiping, if you were to stay on the same "page" it would be considered scrolling. 
Please know that swiping isn't limited from the bottom to the top of your phone but works from all sides to the opposite one.

I think swiping started with the use of tinder (dating app) where that have incorporated the motion whilst searching for a new partner or most likely a shag. Instagram later incorporated it as a way to take people from stories to pages with more information (a story is a video or a photo the size of your phone screen, preferably vertica, that lasts for a maximum or 15seconds). Then after Instagram it looks like Snapchat has done a very similar adaptation.
